source: Six learner attempts saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Recall of personal commands in positive/negative action sequences
summary: Longer command initially mixed infinitive probarla and puedes dime. Focused correction followed by correct feminine sequence and masculine transfer. Positive/negative object placement then correct for both genders. Publices needed qu correction, retained in immediate feminine transfer. Primero spelling slips and command accents supplied. No new grammar or vocabulary introduced.

observations.learnerText: primero probarla, puedes dime si esta lista
observations.correctedText: Primero pruébala; luego dime si está lista.
observations.outcome: First clause used infinitive probarla for requested command, and second mixed puedes with command dime. Tutor supplied two direct commands pruébala and dime, contrasting probarla/pruébala. No separate puedes decirme rule was taught.
Correct personal command and feminine object after focused model; accent supplied.

observations.learnerText: primero pruebala, luego dime si esta lista
observations.correctedText: Primero pruébala; luego dime si está lista.
observations.outcome: Correct full retry with two direct commands, attached la and feminine lista. Accents supplied.

observations.learnerText: primeor pruebalo, luego dime si esta listo
observations.correctedText: Primero pruébalo; luego dime si está listo.
observations.outcome: Correct masculine lo/listo transfer and command stem. Primero letter transposition and accents supplied; no grammatical correction.
Correct affirmative attached lo and negative pre-verbal lo, both matching logo. Publices needed c → qu before e; revísalo accent supplied.

Correct feminine transfer in both commands and retained qu after immediate correction. Extra letter in Primero and revísala accent supplied. Earlier positive-versus-negative pronoun placement retained.

nextSteps: Recheck direct commands without fresh models during ordinary work
Revisit publiques spelling after a gap
Keep future units practical and small; add a further command lexeme when useful
assessmentNote: Correct immediate retries and grammatical transfers recorded separately from initial errors. Repeated spelling corrections do not erase correct command placement or agreement; no durable mastery inferred.
